dept_response: Officers responded to the area and determined no crime had occurred; after being attacked, an officer-involved animal shooting occurred; animal control officers transported the dog to a facility for treatment.
summary: LAPD officers responded to a domestic incident call in the Green Meadows neighborhood on Thursday morning. As they returned to their vehicle, three unrestrained dogs emerged from a property and charged at them; one dog attacked an officer, resulting in a shooting. The officer was bitten on the leg and taken to a hospital for treatment of puncture wounds.
A sheriff's deputy fired a gun at a dog during a pack attack in northwest Charlotte that injured four people.

agency_name: Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department - Crescenta Valley Station
dept_response: Sheriff's Captain Ryan Vienna commended the deputies for attempting non-lethal de-escalation with a Taser before using the firearm; an administrative review of the deputy's decision is pending.
summary: Los Angeles County Sheriff's deputies were arresting a grand theft suspect near Sunland Park Recreation Center when the suspect's pit bull attacked them. After a Taser proved ineffective, a deputy fired on the dog, which survived and was taken to a veterinary hospital for treatment.

dept_response: The sheriff's office says the incident remains under investigation and officials are reviewing the circumstances.
summary: A Hopkins County Sheriff's Office deputy shot and killed a dog while serving a high-risk felony warrant on Wednesday. According to the sheriff's office, the dog lunged at the deputy after pushing past a resident, prompting the deputy to fire his weapon.
An officer in Allentown shot a loose dog after it attacked three people.

dept_response: The incident was referred to Twin Falls County Sheriff's Office for an independent investigation, consistent with established practice for officer-involved incidents.
summary: A Twin Falls police officer shot a large Rottweiler on Wednesday afternoon, August 12, 2026, at approximately 1:30 p.m. while visiting a residence as part of an active investigation. The dog ran toward the officer after he knocked on the door; according to police, the officer discharged his duty weapon, striking the animal. The dog was transported to a veterinary office, treated, and released to its owner.
Police killed a dog described as having lunged or bitten an officer during or after a car chase near Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.
Deputies in Graham, Washington killed an aggressive dog near the scene where a 5-year-old girl was found dead after disappearing.

dept_response: Police said the dog would be tested for rabies because of its aggressive behavior; no arrests or charges were filed.
summary: Waterloo police responded to a report of two dogs fighting in a backyard near 4th and Locust streets on Aug. 19, 2026. As the owners tried to separate them the larger dog became aggressive and an officer shot and killed it; both owners were bitten and no person was struck by gunfire.

dept_response: Internal Affairs Unit conducting internal review of the use of force.
summary: A Cobb County sheriff's deputy fatally shot a dog while serving an arrest warrant on Wednesday. Authorities said the dog was behaving aggressively at the time.
A police officer fatally shot a dog described as "aggressive" in Annapolis. It had bitten two people and two dogs before charging at a police officer

dept_response: Phoenix Police department stated the officer shot the dog after it reportedly bit him and lunged at him a second time while he was searching a backyard.
summary: A Phoenix Police officer shot a dog early Sunday morning during a burglary investigation while searching a backyard near 7th Avenue and Broadway Road. Officers said the dog bit the officer and lunged at him a second time before being shot.

dept_response: Sheriff's Office said the sergeant fired to protect himself because of the earlier attack and the dog charging at him; investigation continuing and will be reviewed with the District Attorney's Office.
summary: A Fulton County Sheriff's sergeant fired at a German Shepherd that charged at him while deputies were investigating a report of a suspicious person trespassing on property in St. Johnsville. The sergeant said he fired in self-defense due to the dog's aggressive behavior and a previous dog bite incident involving a deputy.

dog_breed_reported: golden retriever, Saint Bernard, and poodle mix
dept_response: LAPD said officers asked the woman to secure the dog; after she briefly closed and reopened the door, the dog exited and charged at an officer, who opened fire. LAPD's Force Investigation Division is investigating.
summary: LAPD officers responded to a report of a screaming woman at an apartment building in Canoga Park on June 13, 2026. Officers shot and killed Jameson, a 2-year-old golden retriever/Saint Bernard/poodle mix, after the dog allegedly charged at an officer when it exited the apartment during the welfare check.

A San Bernardino County sheriff's deputy fatally shot a homeowner's dog while investigating reports of a stolen vehicle. The homeowner contends the deputy should not have been on the property, particularly since the vehicle was located elsewhere.

dept_response: Deputies deployed pepper spray multiple times and deployed a Taser before firing; they immediately began emergency medical care after neutralizing the dog, using first aid kits to pack neck wounds and maintain victim consciousness until EMS arrived.
summary: A Richland County Sheriff's Deputy responded to an active dog mauling on April 27, 2026, where a woman was under attack by a Pitbull mix named "Clyde" that had already killed a smaller dog. After pepper spray and a Taser proved ineffective and the dog advanced toward a deputy, the officer fired a single shot, killing the dog and allowing emergency medical care to begin.
A Pecos officer shot a dog after it reportedly attacked multiple people, one of whom required surgery.

dept_response: Police concluded the officer's actions complied with Wisconsin law and police policy; they stated the officer's actions were taken to prevent serious injury to a person and continued attacks on another dog, and noted that other force options could have worsened the outcome.
summary: A Fox Crossing police officer shot a rottweiler multiple times during an active attack at Fritsch Park after the unleashed dog attacked a smaller dog and appeared to be attacking a person; the rottweiler died as a result of the shooting. The police department investigated and determined the officer's actions complied with state law and departmental policy.

dept_response: The Bergen County Prosecutor's Office is continuing the investigation. The New Jersey Attorney General's Office was informed and designated the BCPO to lead the investigation.
summary: A Bogota police officer fired a weapon at a dog that lunged at him while responding to a report of the animal biting a 17-year-old girl on Palisades Avenue and Linwood Avenue. The dog survived the shooting.

dept_response: The officer was treated at Broward General Medical Center for minor, non-life threatening injuries sustained from the bite. Police investigated the incident through the department's Animal Crimes Unit.
summary: A Fort Lauderdale Police officer responded to a call about a large dog that had entered a home and killed a pet rabbit. When the officer encountered the dog, it attacked and bit the officer on the forearm; the officer then fired, hitting the dog, which fled but was later found by Broward County Animal Control.

dept_response: Officers initially responded to a hit-and-run involving a sedan. About an hour later, officers responded to a stolen vehicle report and located the vehicle. As officers wrapped up the investigation, a large pit bull escaped from a fenced yard, charged at officers, and lunged at an officer who then fired one round and killed the animal. Police said the dog was not connected to the investigation and no one was injured.
summary: An Oroville police officer shot and killed a pit bull that escaped from a nearby fenced yard and charged at officers while they were wrapping up a hit-and-run investigation on July 29, 2026. Police said the dog attacked officers after one officer attempted to stop it with a Taser, and no officers or bystanders were injured.

dept_response: Body camera footage was released by LRPD showing the events leading to the shooting.
summary: Little Rock Police Officer Brandon Foster-Todd shot and killed a dog on Country Club Boulevard while responding to a reported battery call. Witnesses described the police response escalating quickly in the residential Heights neighborhood.

dept_response: Deputy commanding dog to stop before shooting; immediately provided medical aid to victim after shooting.
summary: An LA County Sheriff's Deputy shot and killed a pit bull that was attacking an unresponsive man in a locked front yard in Lancaster. The deputy attempted commands before firing; the victim was taken to a hospital in stable condition.
Topeka police shot and killed a dog after two people were bitten.

dept_response: The officer was placed on administrative leave per protocol; Pennsylvania State Police investigated. The York County District Attorney determined the officer was justified in using lethal force to defend himself from an immediate threat.
summary: A York City Police officer responding to a disorderly conduct call at 300 West Philadelphia Street encountered a pit bull mix that escaped from an apartment and pursued him. The officer retreated and fired three times, killing the dog, but also accidentally striking the dog's owner in the leg; the District Attorney found the officer's use of force justified based on video evidence showing the dog was snarling, showing teeth, and closing within 4-5 feet of the officer.

dept_response: Officer placed on administrative leave, then resigned during the investigation. The Ozaukee County District Attorney declined to file criminal charges; the officer was issued a Class C civil forfeiture (non-criminal citation) for mistreating animals.
summary: A Thiensville police officer fired 16 rounds at two unattended dogs observed near North Cedarburg and Highland roads in Mequon on April 23. One dog was killed; the second was injured and later rescued after 17 days, sustaining bullet wounds to the hip and back end requiring multiple surgeries.
A Norfolk officer shot and killed a dog while responding to a call on a Sunday afternoon.

dept_response: Monroe County Sheriff's Office stated the dog charged aggressively at the deputy; after unsuccessful attempts to kick the dog away, the deputy discharged his firearm.
summary: A Monroe County Sheriff's deputy shot a German Shepard mix during a family trouble call in Frenchtown Township on May 5, 2026. According to the sheriff's office, the dog charged aggressively at deputy Garret Kaatz; after unsuccessful attempts to stop it, Kaatz fired his gun, fatally wounding the dog.

dept_response: Officers opened fire on the dog after it continued to attack its owner despite attempts to restrain it.
summary: A 52-year-old man was attacked by his own dog at his Bowie home on Sunday morning around 7:30 a.m. Bowie police officers arrived and opened fire on the dog after it continued attacking the man despite attempts to restrain it; the man was taken to a hospital in serious condition.

dept_response: LAPD stated officers encountered a vicious dog that attacked an officer; the officer was bitten and injured, requiring hospitalization.
summary: During a traffic stop and bomb squad investigation in Sun Valley, LAPD officers fatally shot a dog that officers said attacked one of them. The attacked officer was bitten and fell backward, hitting his head on the pavement, and was hospitalized.

dept_response: Supervisor Deputy Richard Petkovsek responded to the scene and assisted with the injured dog; the department notified Palm Coast Animal Control.
summary: Deputy Devrin Perdue responded to a welfare check at a duplex on Farraday Lane after a 911 caller reported two dogs left outside in shock collars; as Perdue walked back to his vehicle, the black dog (a two-and-a-half-year-old labrador-pit bull mix named Bear) ran toward him aggressively and jumped at him, prompting Perdue to fire two rounds, striking the dog. Bear underwent surgery for lung injuries and is receiving care at animal hospitals; several children witnessed the shooting from a screened-in porch.

dept_response: As is standard operating procedure, MCSO will complete a thorough investigation into the incident.
summary: A Monroe County sheriff's deputy responding to a welfare check at a Pittsford home was attacked and bitten by a dog that charged from the house's breezeway. The deputy fired two rounds from an agency-issued firearm and killed the dog; the deputy suffered a puncture wound and was treated and released at a hospital.

Chicago police shot a dog after it bit a 25-year-old woman and a 15-year-old girl inside a residence in the 4200 block of West Cullerton Street in North Lawndale early on July 26, 2026. Both victims were hospitalized in serious condition; police did not say whether the dog survived.

A Chicago police officer fatally shot a dog on South Ashland Avenue in the West Pullman neighborhood after two dogs attacked a woman, per CPD. Date not confirmed; possibly distinct from the North Lawndale shooting.

dept_response: Special Investigations Response Team (SIRT) investigating
summary: Baltimore police responded to the 6500 block of Hartwait Street in Southeast Baltimore around 3 p.m. on March 6, 2026 for a reported dog bite and found the injured owner. The unrestrained dog charged an officer and two officers fired; an officer suffered a ricochet gunshot wound to the foot. The dog was later euthanized. SIRT is investigating.
A Baltimore police officer fatally shot a dog on West Franklin Street after it attacked two women and their pet, around late July 2026. Distinct from the March 2026 Hartwait Street shooting.
An NYPD officer shot a pit bull that was attacking its owner (a woman) in Far Rockaway, Queens, on the night of March 31, 2026; the dog was killed. Some outlets reported two dogs were shot.
Winters police shot and killed a dog while responding to a domestic-violence call near the Railroad Avenue bridge on Sunday, May 31, 2026.
A Canandaigua police officer shot and killed a dog on May 6, 2026 after it seriously injured its owner and then charged the officer.

Portland police responded to a home on SE Stark Street near 136th Avenue on a Sunday afternoon in early March 2026 after callers reported a dog attacking people inside. Officers shot the dog, which was still attacking on arrival; multiple people were treated for injuries. (Exact date approximate.)

dept_response: Per the family, officers left the scene without a written report; CPD did not respond to requests for comment or bodycam footage
summary: Alicia Wheeler-Stevens called 911 on Tuesday, February 10, 2026 reporting a suspected break-in at her home on West North Bend Road in College Hill, Cincinnati. When officers arrived, one of her dogs escaped the house and an officer shot it in the head. The dog, Max, survived; the owners are seeking accountability and roughly $3,000 in vet bills.

dept_response: State police conducting an internal investigation; DA said bodycam showed the trooper was attacked repeatedly before firing
summary: A Pennsylvania State Police trooper conducting a welfare check on a child at a home on Renovo Road in Allison Township, Clinton County, in February 2026 was attacked by a dog when the door opened and shot and killed it. The family says the trooper pushed into the house; the DA said bodycam showed repeated attacks. State police are investigating internally.

A Honolulu police officer fatally shot a pit bull that charged at him during an HPD operation in Kalaeloa around 6:35 p.m. on July 22, 2026. The dog fled and was later found dead. One officer was reported injured.

During a homeless-encampment cleanup near Bradley Avenue and Montague Street in Pacoima around 10:45 a.m. on April 28, 2026, a loose dog repeatedly bit a sanitation worker and an LAPD officer. The officer shot and killed the dog; the officer and worker were hospitalized in stable condition.

dept_response: Sheriff's office released bodycam footage after online attention
summary: Callaway County sheriff's deputies went to a home on Tate Drive near Auxvasse around 4:14 p.m. on July 14, 2026 to serve a failure-to-appear arrest warrant. Two dogs approached; one behaved aggressively. Pepper spray failed, and when the dog charged again Deputy Zach Hubbard shot and killed it. Bodycam footage was released.
